title: Logical Identity Reductions (Premature Boolean Optimizations)
pattern: Manually applying algebraic boolean reductions (like de Morgan's laws) to simplify logical expressions to "save" logical operators at the expense of readability.
why_bad: It forces the reader to pause and mentally expand the logical terms, raising the cognitive barrier. Compilers automatically perform boolean optimization, so manual rewrite of logic for speed is useless.
detection: Rewriting simple conditions to logical equivalents that use fewer operators but are less direct in their domain representation.
counterexample: Domain logic that naturally maps to the reduced form. `Context-dependent`.
